title: Vintage Gibson SG Standard Value Guide: Prices By Year
description: SG Standard values from $2,500 to $23,000 by year through 1979. I explain small guards, lyre Vibrolas, original humbuckers and repaired neck joints.
h1: Vintage Gibson SG Standard Value Guide
alt: Cherry SG Standard body with two humbuckers, four knobs and a sideways vibrato in a red-lined case

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Standard Worth?
faqs.a: Vintage Gibson SG Standard reference values run from $2,500 to $3,000 for typical 1970s cherry guitars to $13,000 to $24,350 for early small-guard examples, as of October 2026. Original humbuckers, the factory vibrato and an unbroken neck put the strongest examples near the top of their group.

faqs.q: Does A Small Guard Always Mean An Early SG Standard?
faqs.a: No. Small guards return on the 1970s Standard alongside later neck construction, block inlays and different bridge configurations. A 1960s small guard and a 1970s small guard do not establish the same market category.

faqs.q: Does This Guide Price Walnut Standards?
faqs.a: The later 1960s large-guard group includes cherry and walnut. The 1970s $2,500 to $3,000 band is cherry only; non-cherry catalog finishes are excluded from that band.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Change Gibson SG Standard Value?
faqs.a: Yes. The ranges assume the original finish described in the condition notes. A full refinish changes the collector category, so I assess the finish work, retained parts and repairs individually. The reduction depends on the quality of the work, era and retained original parts.

faqs.q: How Can I Get My Gibson SG Standard Appraised?
faqs.a: Send clear front and back photographs, both sides of the headstock, the pickups, bridge, case and any known repairs. Keep removed original parts with the instrument and include the history you know. Those details support an individual appraisal.
